primary_task: Write (or review) Go acceptance tests for a Terraform Plugin Framework provider resource using terraform-plugin-testing patterns (TestCase/TestStep, ConfigStateChecks, import, disappears, CheckDestroy).

requirements.name: read/write/edit files
requirements.evidence: Use when writing, reviewing, or debugging provider acceptance tests
requirements.basis: "read": "read files in the working directory ..."; "write": "create and overwrite files"; "edit": "edit existing files and Jupyter notebooks"

requirements.name: go toolchain + terraform-plugin-testing / terraform-plugin-framework modules
requirements.evidence: Patterns for writing acceptance tests using [terraform-plugin-testing](https://github.com/hashicorp/terraform-plugin-testing) with the [Plugin Framework](https://github.com/hashicorp/terraform-plugin-framework).
requirements.basis: "bash": "... install packages from the open registries (... go modules ... GitHub release downloads) ..."; "egress_allow": [... "proxy.golang.org", "sum.golang.org" ...]

requirements.name: terraform CLI
requirements.evidence: The framework runs each TestStep through: **plan → apply → refresh → final plan**.

requirements.name: target provider API credentials (EXAMPLE_API_KEY)
requirements.evidence: if os.Getenv("EXAMPLE_API_KEY") == "" { t.Fatal("EXAMPLE_API_KEY must be set for acceptance tests") }
requirements.basis: lacks: "accounts, logins, API keys or credentials for external services other than the listed connectors and GitHub"

notes: Reading taken: the deliverable is the test code (writing/reviewing); the document never orders the agent to execute the acceptance tests. Other reading: if the request is to run/debug the acceptance tests (TF_ACC), they create real resources against the provider's API and require its credentials (EXAMPLE_API_KEY), which are unavailable, giving BLOCKED (unless the provider's API is GitHub). Go modules and terraform are installable; the source docs host is denied but only cited.
